Figure 4. Microstructure of the composite electrodes with a) inorganic SE and b) polymer-matrix SE. In (a), voids appear between the inorganic SE particles and the AMPs. Cracking or delamination may occur due to the volume change of AMPs during cycling. In (b), intimate contact is realized between the polymer-matrix SE and the AMPs. Voids may appear after cycling because of the plastic deformation of the polymer-matrix SE. c) Schematic energy diagram of the CAMP and sulfide SE. When the μc of the CAMP is higher than the HOMO of the sulfide SE, the sulfide SE is not oxidized and the CAMP/sulfide system is thermodynamically stable (left). If the μc of the CAMP is lower than the HOMO of the sulfide SE, a cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) with a HOMO lower than the μc is required to keep the CAMP/sulfide system stable (middle).
